messages:
julia: ran a 12h mixed-workload sim comparing aggressive prefill vs decode-driven eviction. high-level: prefill -> lower p99 but more steady memory; decode-evict -> more transient allocations, higher fragmentation and OOMs. logs attached.

amit: numbers plz (p50/p95/p99/throughput/ooms)

julia: paste: ```
baseline(prefill-heavy): p50=20ms p95=130ms p99=360ms thpt=820 req/s OOM=1
decode-evict:         p50=19ms p95=140ms p99=440ms thpt=790 req/s OOM=6
```
p99 regressed ~22%, OOMs x6.

sara: where is fragmentation concentrated? slab-level, slot-level?

julia: slab-level. lots of 512B-8KB entries from prefills creating holes; decode-evict ends up scattering small live allocations across slabs causing fragmentation growth over time.

amit: we tried a 2MB soft cap per request last cycle. did that stay?

julia: yes. but decode-evict means more ad-hoc allocs that push into new slabs despite the cap. cap alone doesn't stop interleaving across slabs.

omar: idea: hybrid heat-aware prefill. keep a lightweight prefill for hot prefixes to avoid transient bursts, and for tail prefixes limit prefill and enforce slab-local reservation.

sara: agree. also propose per-request slab budget: max N slabs per request. prevents one tail request from fragmenting entire worker.

julia: prototype rule: ```
if hotset.contains(prefix): prefill_limit=64KB; slab_budget=4
else: prefill_limit=8KB; slab_budget=2
```
sim results: p99 improved ~8% vs decode-only and OOMs back near baseline.

amit: any kernel interactions? different kernels have different temporary workspace requirements which can change effective fragmentation/OOM behaviour.

julia: ran with two kernels: fused-attn (higher temp alloc) and tiled-attn (lower). fused bumped OOMs another ~30% on decode-evict. so kernel_temp_overhead must factor into slab_budget.

sara: propose runtime formula: cap_per_request = base_cap + kernel_overhead[kernel] + quant_adjust. store kernel_overhead table per model/seq_len.

omar: also a compact-on-high-frag heuristic: sample slabs every T seconds, if slab_frag_pct > threshold then compact that slab between batches. selective compaction avoids global stalls.

julia: compaction numbers: selective compaction of slabs with >60% slack and >2 fragmented runs reduced OOMs by ~55% in sim, cost ~2-4ms per compaction event. worth it if we gate by latency impact.

amit: rollout plan? canary with conservative defaults and observability.

julia: propose rollout steps:
- implement heat-aware prefill (freq-sketch hotset)
- per-request slab_budget adjusted by kernel_overhead table
- selective slab compaction when slab_frag_pct > 60% for >Y sec
- canary 1% dedicated pool, watch p99/oom_count/kv.slab_fragmentation_pct

sara: add an opt-out to disable compaction per route if latency spikes >5% for that route. also add CI sim that reproduces mixed prefill/decode traffic. previous CI missed this.

omar: i'll run microbenchmarks to populate kernel_overhead table (model x kernel x seq).

julia: action items:
- julia: PR w/ heat-aware prefill + selective compaction + sim scenario (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- omar: kernel microbenchmarks + overhead table (ETA: next week)
- sara: add kv.slab_fragmentation_pct metric + allocation trace instrumentation
- amit: schedule 1% canary after PRs merge

eng-bot: created issue #3125 kv-hybrid-prefill-heat-aware-evict assigned to julia

sara: minor: include a regression test injecting long-tail sequences and alternating kernel paths; that caught a prior OOM.

julia: yep will add. will also stash simulation artifacts in the perf bucket.

amit: thanks team. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
